answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring every identity to complete a verifiable sequence of modular squarings, where each result depends on the one before it. GPUs can run separate clone computations concurrently, but cannot parallelize away the sequential work or reduce the elapsed-time floor for any one identity. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently; the nectar of many clones still faces this physical bottleneck, whether carried by a gale or set in opal.
